recent_posts.title: GitHub's reliability crisis and the role of AI-driven growth
recent_posts.summary: GitHub's reliability has deteriorated sharply, with 257 incidents tracked between May 2025 and April 2026, including 48 major outages. GitHub Actions alone suffered 57 outages in that period. The root cause, per GitHub's CTO, is the explosive growth of agentic AI workflows demanding 30x the platform's designed capacity. High-profile users like Mitchell Hashimoto (Ghostty) and the Zig project have migrated away. Compounding the scaling crisis are engineering failures like an incomplete feature flag that silently reverted thousands of merged pull requests. Microsoft's absorption of GitHub into its CoreAI org and commercial pressure around Copilot are seen as contributing factors. GitHub has declared an 'availability first' mandate, but community patience is running thin as comparable platforms like GitLab and npm handle the same AI-driven growth without comparable disruptions.

recent_posts.title: The reality of being a senior engineering manager
recent_posts.summary: The transition from engineering manager to senior engineering manager is less about managing larger teams and more about shaping the systems and environments in which execution happens. Senior EMs must operate through influence rather than authority, building trust across organizational boundaries, aligning stakeholders without formal power, and coaching leaders rather than individual contributors. Key distinctions include: impact defined by organizational scope not org size, invisible work like pre-aligning stakeholders and resolving misaligned incentives, maintaining technical depth at a higher altitude to make system-level bets, and using directors to amplify systems rather than rescue them. The role also evolves in the context of AI-native systems, where senior EMs increasingly act as integrators across people, platforms, and intelligent systems. The core shift is moving from personal execution excellence to ensuring the entire system executes well.

recent_posts.title: Four practices that compound into lasting software engineering career growth
recent_posts.summary: A 16-year software engineering veteran shares four compounding practices for career growth: deliberate writing and documentation, building community, structured experimentation, and managing imposter syndrome. Drawing from experience across IT service firms, product companies, and a startup, the author argues that technical excellence alone is insufficient. Key insights include keeping a personal learning log, using code reviews as learning tools, blocking unstructured exploration time, and reframing imposter syndrome as something to manage rather than eliminate.

recent_posts.title: How Cloudflare rebuilt Next.js in a weekend using agentic coding
recent_posts.summary: Cloudflare rebuilt Next.js in a single weekend using Claude in OpenCode, spending just $1,100 in tokens. The result, called vinext, is a Vite plugin that reimplements the Next.js API surface natively for Cloudflare's infrastructure. It builds production apps up to 4x faster and produces 57% smaller client bundles. Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht frames this as the next evolution of open-source forking, made dramatically cheaper and faster by agentic coding. He argues the build-vs-buy equation has fundamentally changed, shifting engineers from writing code to directing AI agents through plans and specs. While not every team should rebuild everything, Knecht believes agentic coding will spur a wave of purpose-built replacements for aging open-source projects.

recent_posts.title: Six software engineering buzzwords to replace with precise language
recent_posts.summary: Six overused software engineering buzzwords are examined and critiqued: 'AI-powered', '10x engineer', 'tech debt', 'vibe coding', 'velocity', and 'shift left'. Each term is analyzed for how it lost precision and became counterproductive, with input from senior engineers and engineering leaders. Concrete replacements are suggested for each — for example, replacing 'AI-powered' with specific technique and outcome descriptions, '10x engineer' with 'high-leverage engineer', and 'shift left' with explicit, actionable language like 'test earlier' or 'flag security issues before code review'. The core argument is that vague buzzwords widen the gap between technical and business stakeholders rather than bridging it, and that precise language leads to better decision-making.

recent_posts.title: AI coding tool costs are rising as agentic usage explodes
recent_posts.summary: AI coding tool costs are rising sharply as agentic workflows consume far more tokens than traditional chat-based interactions. Vendors like GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and Windsurf have moved from flat subscriptions to token-based billing, introduced usage multipliers, and tightened rate limits. Internal data suggests GitHub Copilot's serving costs have nearly doubled since January 2025. Engineering managers now face a choice between absorbing higher cloud AI costs or shifting to local LLM inference, while also needing to justify AI spend with concrete ROI rather than anecdotal productivity gains.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic's seven weeks of silence over Claude Code degradation eroded developer trust
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic silently degraded Claude Code for seven weeks through three engineering missteps: reducing reasoning effort from high to medium on March 4, a bug discarding reasoning history mid-session on March 26, and a system prompt capping responses at 25 words on April 16. Users noticed declining performance — including more errors, instruction-following failures, and riskier 'edit-first' behavior — but received no communication until a postmortem appeared after the final fix on April 20. Engineering leaders and developers argue that silence amplified speculation and eroded trust, and that real-time status updates during incidents are more valuable than detailed postmortems published weeks later.

recent_posts.title: Five architectural patterns for deploying generative AI in legacy codebases
recent_posts.summary: Lessons from deploying generative AI on a 70,000-file legacy codebase reveal five architectural patterns for success: (1) use targeted line replacements instead of full-file rewrites to stay within model context limits; (2) convert visual legacy design documents into machine-readable plain text for better AI context; (3) add an agentic planning layer before any code is written; (4) run multiple generation passes and enforce strict output formatting to stabilize probabilistic AI output; (5) modernize CI/CD pipelines to fully automated scripts, since AI cannot interact with manual or proprietary build steps. The core insight is that AI failures in legacy environments stem from infrastructure unreadiness, not model intelligence.

recent_posts.title: Tokenmaxxing and the search for AI metrics that matter
recent_posts.summary: Token usage — dubbed 'tokenmaxxing' — is emerging as the AI era's equivalent of measuring lines of code: easy to track, easy to game, and disconnected from real productivity. Meta's internal token-consumption leaderboard sparked industry backlash after going public. Engineering leaders share alternative frameworks: a four-level 'cognitive delegation' model inspired by the executive chef analogy (measuring how much mental work engineers offload to AI agents), and a self-reporting approach that works in high-trust organizations. Experts agree token usage is a useful early adoption signal but a poor productivity metric, and that combined metrics — not a single number — are needed. No consensus exists yet on the right replacement, and tooling to connect token spend to shipping outcomes is still immature.

recent_posts.title: The reality of being a staff engineer
recent_posts.summary: A staff engineer at Crunchyroll shares what the role actually looks like in 2026. The key insight: the shift from senior to staff is horizontal, not vertical — it's about going wide across teams rather than deep on one team's problems. The real work is coordination, writing, and relationship-building across organizational boundaries, not just coding. The author also covers how AI tools (Copilot with MCP integrations, Datadog notebooks) are changing not just personal productivity but the scope of staff engineer responsibilities — including leading a 12-week AI-native engineering training program. Core skills distilled: comfort with ambiguity, clear writing, knowing when to delegate, and cross-org relationship building.

top_posts.title: Best AI coding tools for 2026 ranked and compared
top_posts.summary: A comprehensive 2026 evaluation of AI coding tools, judged not just on code generation but on deployment awareness, architectural intelligence, and alignment with DORA/Progressive Delivery principles. The top six tools—Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot Workspace, Windsurf, Sourcegraph Cody, and Tabnine—are assessed across full-context awareness, workflow integration, multi-model orchestration, and their ability to help teams ship safely at velocity. Honorable mentions cover specialists like Augment Code, Amazon Q Developer, Vercel v0, Lovable, OpenAI Codex CLI, and Google Antigravity. Each tool's strengths, limitations, pricing, and 2026 outlook are detailed, with a recurring theme: the best tools are evolving from code helpers into deployment partners.

top_posts.title: Software engineering leaders need a shopkeeper mentality
top_posts.summary: Engineering leaders often fall into a trap of reactive, task-focused work that crowds out broader situational awareness. The 'shopkeeper mentality' is a leadership framework that encourages intentional, regular scanning across people, work quality, and team signals — much like a store owner surveying their shop each morning. Grounded in neuroscience (the antagonism between the task-positive and default mode brain networks), the approach argues that broad awareness cannot happen as a side effect of execution; it must be scheduled as dedicated time. Practical techniques for remote/hybrid environments include a daily 30-minute 'manager gathering time' reviewing Slack and email for patterns, monitoring work output for quality shifts, creating low-stakes social touchpoints, and periodically reviewing key domains like team wellbeing, strategic progress, and peer relationships. The post also warns against two failure modes: micromanagement (confusing responsibility with control) and over-delegation (forgetting that accountability doesn't transfer with work).

top_posts.title: JetBrains goes all-in on agents with Central
top_posts.summary: JetBrains has announced Central, a unified agentic platform designed to govern, orchestrate, and manage AI agents across development teams. Built around three pillars — governance and policy enforcement, cloud infrastructure for agent execution, and a semantic context layer using AST-based code intelligence — Central aims to bridge the gap between AI adoption and measurable productivity gains. Key features include intelligent model routing, support for third-party agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini CLI) via the open Agent Client Protocol, and a hybrid pricing model combining per-seat subscriptions with pay-as-you-go agentic execution and BYOK support. However, Central launches amid trust concerns: JetBrains faced backlash last year over mid-contract pricing changes, and pricing for Central remains unannounced. The platform also coincides with the sunsetting of Code With Me, raising questions about JetBrains' commitment to non-agentic features. Engineering leaders are advised to carefully map the growing JetBrains portfolio — which now includes Junie, Koog, Grazie, Mellum, Air, and Air Team — before committing.
